HOW PUNJAB DIFFERS FROM FBISE, AND WHY THIS FILE LOOKS DIFFERENT
FBISE publishes Student Learning Outcomes with its own alphanumeric codes, and
every note and question we generate points at the outcome it was written for.
Punjab publishes no coded outcome matrix. PCTB holds curriculum authority through
textbooks and notified schemes of studies; PBCC sets the paper pattern and the
annual pairing scheme; the nine BISE boards run the exams. The federal NCC SLO
frameworks on ncc.gov.pk are FBISE's, not Punjab's, and tagging Punjab content
with federal codes would be a lie a Punjab student could catch.
What the 2023 PCTB editions DO carry is the outcomes themselves: every chapter
opens with a box headed "Student's learning outcomes (SLOs)", printed verbatim.
Those are the examinable units. They are read out of the books, given codes we
mint (PJ-PHY-10-C10-S03), and stored with origin='textbook_slo'. Where a chapter
prints none, as with an Urdu lesson, its topics or the lesson itself stand in,
with origin='textbook_topic' and a T in the code. See migration 0035.
ONE CATALOGUE FOR ALL NINE BOARDS. The client confirmed and PBCC's own
notifications agree: curriculum, textbooks and paper pattern are uniform across
Lahore, Rawalpindi, Multan, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Sargodha, Bahawalpur,
Sahiwal and Dera Ghazi Khan. Only past papers differ, so only past papers are
sourced per board.
EVERYTHING HERE IS A SCAN. Unlike FBISE's text PDFs, every Punjab document
below is a scanned image: pdftotext returns zero characters. Extraction reads
the pages with a vision model instead: scripts/extract-punjab-contents.mjs for
each contents page, scripts/extract-punjab-outcomes.mjs for inside each chapter,
then scripts/build-punjab-catalogue.mjs into data/punjab/catalogue.json.
NOT REDISTRIBUTED. These are the boards' documents, fetched into content/punjab/
which is gitignored, exactly as content/fbise/ is. What lives in git is the
structured JSON we derive.
The syllabus itself, and the thing everything else is grounded in. PCTB's own
site (pctb.punjab.gov.pk) refuses connections from outside Pakistan, so these
are fetched by hand and dropped into content/punjab/textbooks/.
Only the 2023 editions ("Based on Revised National Curriculum of Pakistan
2023") are used. File names are {subject}-{class}.pdf, with -ur for an
Urdu-medium copy. Each book also carries its own pairing scheme and model
paper at the back, which is more current than the model papers below.
SUPERSEDED: elearn.punjab.gov.pk. Its chapter tree matched the textbooks line
by line, but the pre-2023 textbooks: Biology 9 there has nine chapters, the
2023 book has eleven. The first catalogue was built from it and was wrong for
exactly that reason. Do not use it as a source of structure.

_comment: Approved by the client (Adnan), via the colleague who supplied them, on 11 September
2026, because the 2023 editions could not be found. Two different uses:
olderEditions.phy-9-ur: The only Physics 9 in hand: National Curriculum 2006, 2018 print. It IS the Class 9 Physics syllabus in the catalogue, 9 units with their printed outcomes. Its units 8 and 9 (thermal properties, transfer of heat) overlap the 2023 Physics 10's chapters 10 and 11.
olderEditions.phy-10-ur, bio-9-ur, chem-9-ur, cs-9-ur,: Different syllabus from the 2023 English books, so they define nothing. Used only to give an Urdu name to a chapter that survived into the new book, matched by title (scripts/build-punjab-catalogue.mjs, matchUrduChapters).

_comment: Model papers stand in for FBISE's Table of Specification: they show the
sections, the mark distribution and the question types the board actually
sets. Gujranwala publishes the full matric set openly and the pattern is
province-wide, so one board's copy serves all nine.
These files carry a 2016 creation date in their metadata. Treat them as the
structure rather than the current session's paper until a newer notified
pattern is in hand: PBCC has since directed that 25% of the paper be
analytical and conceptual, which these predate.
Which subjects belong to which group, and the marks each carries. Nine pages,
scanned, notified for the 2025-26 session.
The one thing that genuinely differs per board, and the richest signal we
have. Multan publishes real question papers WITH official answer keys going
back years, which is what lets us weight topics by how often the board has
actually examined them rather than by a declared specification.
Lahore does not publish a searchable archive, so Multan is the default and
Sahiwal the cross-check.
Named here rather than guessed at, so the gap stays visible.
1. PCTB textbooks for the nine subjects, both classes. The grounding corpus.
Blocked only by the geo-restriction on pctb.punjab.gov.pk.
2. The current PBCC pairing scheme. Punjab students plan revision around it,
and no equivalent exists in the FBISE product, so it is a real feature and
not merely a source document.
3. A paper pattern newer than the 2016 model papers, reflecting the 25%
conceptual directive.
